announcement_body.headline: Patch 1.7.3
announcement_body.body:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/cabe4cc8482cf98278f0820d8ecbb561637de7e4.jpg[/img]

Hello drafters, 

We have released Patch 1.7.3 today which includes some fixes and adjustments.

Please note that this changelog will include spoilers for some rarer rooms and late game mechanics.

[h3]Changelog[/h3]
[list]
[*]Fixed problematic spawn points for trophies in a few rooms ([spoiler]Showroom[/spoiler], [spoiler]Tunnel[/spoiler], and [spoiler]Pump Room[/spoiler]) 
[*]Fixed the lighting on one of the books ([spoiler]ANC[/spoiler]) in the library to make the coloring of the cover more consistent.  
[*]Fixed a collider issue on the checkout card in one of the books ([spoiler]ANC[/spoiler]). 
[*]Fixed a few problematic colliders that made some dig spots in the house harder to trigger.
[*]Added a collider to prevent a desk drawer from being clicked on from the wrong side of the desk. 
[*]Added a safety collider in the [spoiler]basement[/spoiler] to prevent players from accidentally clipping through the floor while [spoiler]operating heavy machinery[/spoiler]. 
[*]Restored the right-mouse icon to the above action UI.
[*]Adjusted a few colliders in the [spoiler]basement[/spoiler] to prevent a narrow softlock.
[*]Fixed a softlock that occurred when digging up a buried hint after earning a trophy but not actually picking it up.
[*]Fixed a large number of corner-case bugs associated with the mechanics of one of Guest Bedroom’s upgraded floorplans. 
[*]Adjusted the pages in a letter found in the Study to make page turning more intuitive. 
[*]Fixed a very rare bug that would result in the Toolshed appearing to only contain one item.
[*]Fixed an oversight that caused a blue item to not spawn when its room was drafted as an outer room.
[*][spoiler]Three Day Blessing of the Tinkerer and Chef[/spoiler] gold amounts have been swapped to correctly align their intended blessing thresholds. (This will align with the higher tiers now.)
[*]The list of blessings printed in an issue of [spoiler]Drafting Strategy[/spoiler] has been reordered and reformatted. 
[*]Finally fixed an elusive bug that prevented the [spoiler]Kennel’s[/spoiler] effect from working correctly in The Foundation.
[/list]
[h3]Challenge Mode / Speedrunning Changelog [/h3]

[i]The below changelog includes challenge mode related and other game mechanics and bugs that players will not typically encounter through regular play.[/i]
[list]
[*]Fixed a troublesome bug in Dare Mode that sometimes failed a certain dare involving red rooms when the player used Secret Garden Key or a similar special key ([spoiler]or a berry[/spoiler]) while drafting. 
[*]Fixed a bug that sometimes caused the fourth dare presented to the player to be blank.
[*]Fixed an unintended issue that only flagged the player as having [spoiler]‘been cursed’[/spoiler] after reading the [spoiler]curse[/spoiler] description in the menu. It now sets the flag correctly.  
[*]A certain in-game timer (utilized by players that play on [spoiler]dare and curse[/spoiler] mode and other speed challenges) now doesn’t begin until the player has begun moving on day one.
[*]Addressed several raycast and UI button issues that sometimes caused major bugs when fast clicking in UI menus. This fixed several issues including misaligned inputs (different buttons/floorplans are pressed than the one you clicked), softlocks and glitches within the Drafting UI, [spoiler]Basement Door UI[/spoiler], Regular Door UI, and other ‘Use a key’ UIs. 
[*]Fixed a bug causing the hand cursor to persist beyond drafting after selecting a floorplan quickly.
[*]Fixed an issue that caused HLC to inadvertently be removed from the Draft Pool under certain circumstances. 
[*]Fixed an issue that could unintentionally make Workshop less common after an item interaction under certain circumstances.
[*]The [spoiler]Armory[/spoiler] is no longer incorrectly categorized as a gem room when you begin the day with [spoiler]Mantle of the Knight[/spoiler].
[/list]
The patch is now live on Steam and will be available for Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo Switch 2 players soon.

If you would be interested in helping us test upcoming patches we have a designated space for this in the Laboratory section of our [url=https://discord.gg/BluePrince]Discord[/url] server.

announcement_body.headline: Patch 1.7 - The Accessibility Update
announcement_body.body:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/eee793a7491b6926f919d973950bad99f5bf5706.jpg[/img]

Good Day Drafters, 

Blue Prince’s Patch 1.7 is now available! (Console and Mac players should expect to see this update next week.)

This patch includes our accessibility update alongside a number of fixes for issues reported from the community. 

A full changelog is included below:

[b][h2]1.7 Changelog[/h2][/b]
[b][h3]The Accessibility Update[/h3][/b]
1.7 marks the completion of a large rollout of accessibility features. These features can be accessed via the Accessibility menu and include: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/e58e1b1a45dc40a99b40ee13789eced8e682c469.png[/img]

[b]Color Assist[/b] - A set of tools to provide color clarity to players who have trouble distinguishing some specific colors in the game. In addition to making puzzle colors a bit more vivid, we have also included separate systems to display color patterns, and an even more robust system that displays color labels for objects of inquiry. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/93aeeeeb7fac538ecf81bd30b6ab3a894b5595c3.png[/img]

[b]Remapping [/b]- Yes! Key/button remapping is now supported for both keyboard and controller. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/2ba20c6bad4678b39163bf16e9eec8295e50199e.png[/img]

[b]Cursor Set[/b] -  Options for changing the opacity, style, and size of the game’s reticle and cursor (this is part of our new Motion Assist options.)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/07c7d439c57167b027d5f081ff4ba596b07f958e.png[/img]

[b]Invert Stroll[/b] - This is a feature that will allow players to invert the stroll button functionality. Inverting this means you will move at the faster stroll speed without needing to press/hold a button, and pressing/holding the stroll button will slow you down to a walk.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/98fed33d1928406da5c1d57a6e806696e1712201.png[/img]

[b]Motion Assist[/b] - A consolidated menu of features and settings aimed to reduce motion sickness and sensory conflict: Cursor/Reticle Settings, Look Sensitivity, Field of View, Smooth Look, and Stairs Skip (visually turn off spiral staircase travel.) Each feature is included along with our recommended setting adjustments.

[b][h3]Changelog cont. [/h3][/b]

[i]The patch notes below will include spoilers for some rarer rooms and mechanics.
[/i]
[list]
[*]We have updated the save file architecture again on PS5 to further address an issue with some save files exceeding size limits. 
[*]As part of the Cursor features implemented above, we have redone the way the system handles changing cursors for a smoother visual experience when drafting, picking up items etc.
[*]Fixed several visual bugs in the [spoiler]Precipice[/spoiler] involving geometry from other areas clipping into the area from certain vantage points. 
[*]Fixed some colliders in the [spoiler]Casino[/spoiler] causing players to inadvertently exit a UI screen while trying to pull a lever.  
[*]Added redundant safety checks to avoid potential soft locks that have been reported to occur within the above UI system.
[*]Fixed an issue that was occasionally displaying a phantom Upgrade Disk in the Security terminal list for some players.
[*]Slightly adjusted some factors related to the way Upgrade Disk floorplans are randomly selected to allow for greater variety during challenge runs while simultaneously making it less likely for new players from getting offered upgrades for rooms they have never drafted.
[*]Fixed several bugs related to Powered Duct animations which restored spinning ducts to several rooms. Changing the direction of power in the Boiler Room also no longer breaks these animations. 
[*]Fixed several routing related bugs that could cause certain details and areas of the grounds and house to not be visible when approaching from certain areas. 
[*]Fixed an animation glitch caused by pressing buttons in the Chamber of Mirrors a bit too quickly that led to unexpected panel behaviour. 
[*]Fixed a handful of issues that were previously preventing floorplans from being duplicated by Chamber of Mirrors (some rooms are still excluded for technical reasons but the list is now more extensive.)
[*]Related to the above - the experimental trigger related to terminal access has been reworked to correctly deal with duplicated terminal rooms. 
[*]A stamp in the Mail Room no longer disappears during magnification when a letter is in the foreground. 
[*]Fixed a bug that shut the book whenever you would click on the checkout card of [spoiler]A New Clue[/spoiler] instead of inspecting it.
[*]Fixed a bug that was unintentionally increasing the likelihood of drawing a non-green room in addition to the intended Green Rooms after Greenhouse had been drafted.
[*]Fixed a bug with a particular locker in [spoiler]locker room[/spoiler] that was occasionally not reacting to interaction. 
[*]Fixed a UI typo of “Bedroom” in an item description.
[*]Fixed a text mesh bug that was not rendering asterisks correctly on a [spoiler]late grade[/spoiler] chalkboard.
[*]Updated templating of Observatory’s floorplan text to be more technically accurate and consistent with the game’s templating. (The floorplan now simply has the text “+1 star”)
[*]Fixed incorrect layer assignments on a few more textures causing them to not be rendered when viewed through the magnifying glass.
[*]Added more descriptive clarity for rarity in the [spoiler]wrench[/spoiler] UI during first time use.
[/list]
[b][h3]Very Late Game Changelog including Deep Spoilers (read at your own risk)[/h3][/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed a rare bug in the [spoiler]Conservatory[/spoiler] that was offering players options from [spoiler]“studio floorplans”[/spoiler] and [spoiler]“found floorplans”[/spoiler] that they had not added to their draft pools.
[*]Added a redundancy check to address a glitch which was causing some challenge mode save files to incorrectly load in Bequest mode.
[*]Fixed a corner case material glitch that related to the blessing of the [spoiler]monk that would sometimes affect the art at the bottom of the Foundation.[/spoiler]
[*]Fixed a sacred bug that only accepted the PM but not the AM.
[*]Finally fixed a troublesome late game bug that was causing the drafting system to regard one very rare room as a color it clearly was not.
[*]Fixed a bug causing [spoiler]boat travel[/spoiler] to occasionally not be persistent between days if the cutscene was skipped. 
[*]Fixed a bug caused by exiting door UI during special key use animation in an underground area.
[*]Addressed reports of clipping through the floor in a very late-game area by adding additional safety measures. 
[*]Fixed some issues that were causing unintended step loss and unintentioned geometry overlapping in that same area. 
[*]Fixed some uvmap texture issues in two of the illustrations in that same area. 🐌🎼 
[*]Gambit of the [spoiler]Queen has been rebalanced to grant the player an additional key per trigger.[/spoiler]
[*]Due to several known bugs and issues with [spoiler]R_y_l  Sc____r[/spoiler] (some of which rendered the item functionless), this item’s design has been subtly changed and expanded. The game will now allow players to set the color an additional time per day from the inventory menu, and the method the player “keeps” the item has also been tweaked.
[/list]
This patch will follow for Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo and App Store players. Each platform has varying timescales for approving patches and we expect this to reach players by late next week. 

Blue Prince is Out Now

announcement_body.headline: History Extended - A Year of Blue Prince
announcement_body.body:
Blue Prince launched a year ago today!

To celebrate this noteworthy occasion Trigg & Gusset are releasing a new single, an extended version of ‘History Suspended’ from the Blue Prince OST, reimagined by the dark jazz Dutch duo with a full band. Fittingly, the new track is titled ‘History Extended’.

You can listen to the new track on [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aYyaxGlVk3w ]Youtube[/url] and [url=https://triggandgusset.bandcamp.com/track/history-extended]Bandcamp[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/eeeab800f4ab01866be7ca4231f4d083a44a2ce0.jpg[/img]

Also of note, The Secret Lives of Games, a collective of game developers that have candid conversations with other game creators, are releasing a Blue Prince anniversary episode today featuring Tonda Ros (Obligatory spoiler warning), which will be available to listen to at  https://secretlives.games/. The Secret Lives of Games is an incredible interview/conversational series with over 150 episodes of in depth discussions with some of our absolute favorite developers like Daniel Mullins, Derek Yu, and Terry Cavanagh to name a meager few.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/3f1e3ef0223a636927a18ceb3d5319fd2926cf58.png[/img]

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

It has certainly been a remarkable year for the game, Dogubomb and the team here at Raw Fury and we wanted to take a moment to look back at some of the highlights since the game's release.

Blue Prince launched on 10 April 2025 to positive acclaim from reviewers and players alike. We could not have asked for a better reception and such an outpouring of positive reactions from the public, the press, and our community. In fact, at the time of release, (before Clair Obscure entered the arena) Blue Prince was the best reviewed game of the year!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/c4997d4e7f818911e08fa51061933921c8eb5a1f.png[/img]

In May we encountered the PS5 Save Issue that impacted players deeper into the game. It took a lot of investigation and working alongside Sony to get to the bottom of this issue and we released a number of patches to attempt to rectify this for our PS5 players. We understand that this was a stressful and frustrating time for all involved and was by far the biggest problem we have encountered since Blue Prince launched. That said, we also wish to acknowledge the patience and assistance from the community to help the team narrow in on a fix. Without the information, save files, and bug reports we would not have been able to identify the problem and work towards a solution. We truly appreciate everyone who brought this to our attention, provided further information when requested and trusted our team. 

[previewyoutube=5RNSEeSIqUY;full][/previewyoutube]

In June we released our Accolades Trailer compiling a number of quotes from various outlets that had reviewed Blue Prince since launch. It was fantastic to see these altogether in one place. We also released the Music Room Bundle including Blue Prince and the soundtrack by the incredibly talented Trigg & Gusset and the Mac on Steam version was announced.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/d8b86aa518b67fb91a2cbf8bdf01fc3d7e19f9d2.png[/img]

In July the Games Done Quick crew featured Blue Prince in a manner that we had never imagined seeing it played. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cirrfl1yQ2c  It was great to see so many people tuned in for the event and the foam fingers in the crowd and of course how much money was raised for charity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/8333c4aba62f4226f58d968b59c2cb4d5cceaec9.jpg[/img]

In August, Blue Prince returned to Gamescom alongside many other titles at the Raw Fury Booth. It was also the month that we teamed up with the legendary Daniel Mullins in the creation of the Black and Blue Bundle featuring Blue Prince and his inky black masterpiece, Inscryption.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/a7ebb4bcb9a5533f60044d30c13591b49737543b.png[/img]

September saw the announcement of the first Blue Prince x iam8bit Commissary merch collection. This was something that we had worked on for a long time behind the scenes to get this as perfect as possible. We were thrilled to see this announced and the reception to the collection from the community. The collection included the PS5 physical release, The Red Prince Children's Book, Blue Prince Pin Set, Blue Prince Keychain (blind bag), Blue Prince Basement Key Replica with Stand and the Blue Prince Hardbound Moleskin-style Notebook. September also saw the launch of the Mac on Steam version of Blue Prince.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/d1384269ce162a13ea2d07b2b32aa30a7f6d5b26.png[/img]

In October we announced our second Bundle with Myst from Cyan Worlds. (Seeing these two games side by side just felt right!) Later in October, we also learned that Blue Prince was nominated for 3 awards at the Golden Joysticks: Best Indie Game, Best Storytelling and Ultimate Game of the Year.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/b787a9a8ddcb8a54d5165327bf279e9e138bbda6.png[/img]

November included a lot of award nominations for Blue Prince including:
[list]
[*]The Unity Awards - Best Desktop/Console Game, Best 3D Visuals and The Golden Cube Award
[*]The Indie Game Awards - Most Innovative & Game of the Year
[*]The Game Awards - Best Independent Game and Best Debut Indie Game
[/list]
Alongside these incredible nominations were some award wins as well:
[list]
[*]Aesthetica Short Film Festival Best Game Award
[*]The Golden Joysticks - Best Indie Game
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/090ce5c2cf1d7a2a9a939ada5683a4df44fce962.jpg[/img]

Things did not slow down in December. We saw Blue Prince included in so many Best Games of 2025 lists that it would be impractical to list them all but we want to thank everyone who included us in their list. It really does mean a lot to the entire team to see our small indie game listed alongside some of the giants from this amazing year.

We also launched the second Gift Shop merch collection with iam8bit that includes The Blue Prince Soundtrack (either 2x LP or CD), Secret Garden Key Replica, Swim Bird Plush, Swim Bird pin, Blueprint Desk Mat and a Stamp & Postcard Set. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/d7c55cdf2c89c86e2d89046ff3a32f9824f7dd76.png[/img]

Members of the team attended The Game Awards 2025 as Blue Prince was nominated for Best Independent Game and Best Debut Indie that were both taken home by Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. It was amazing to be nominated and congratulations once again to the other nominees to and to Sandfall Interactive for their historic sweep that night!

Blue Prince did win other awards in December 2025 including: 
[list]
[*]Unity Awards - The Golden Cube Award
[*]The Indie Game Awards - Most Innovative and Game of the Year
[*]2 Latam Indie Awards - Best Innovation and Indie Debut 
[*]NextPlay Awards - Best Puzzle/Strategy Game
[/list]
Blue Prince was also nominated in 4 categories at the IGN Awards, 5 categories on the BAFTA long list and 2 awards at the New York Videogame Critic’s Circle. 

Also in December, Blue Prince launched on the Apple Appstore for Mac.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/d69074206293eeaa0e559a564f70a00b2bd96094.png[/img]

January started off with a bang as Blue Prince was nominated for 5 DICE Awards! We also saw a restock of the Commissary Merch Collection with iam8bit which sold out in record time. We have been blown away by the popularity of this collection and we will let everyone know if we have further restocks.

The Trophy Room continued to fill in February as we were awarded both the community and jury voted Game of the Year awards at the 3rd Annual Thinky Awards. Swiftly followed by wins for Outstanding Achievement for an Independent Game and Outstanding Achievement in Game Design at the DICE Awards.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/40e669000c02b3f963b6fb91d9013d7ad1c5df39.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/fbbc521271c69bcd50ab5b164b9d108493b758ab.png[/img]

March saw Blue Prince arrive on Nintendo Switch 2 when we shadowdropped the game at the Indie World event on 3rd March. 

We had been working hard on this highly requested port of the game for some time, so to see the extremely positive response from the community was fantastic. We were very excited to welcome Nintendo Switch 2 players to the Blue Prince community.

[previewyoutube=s6Xwox34_yU;full][/previewyoutube]

After our inclusion in the BAFTA Long List at the end of 2025 we were delighted to see Blue Prince make the shortlist and was officially nominated for 4 BAFTAs!
[list]
[*]Best Game
[*]Debut Game
[*]Game Design
[*]Narrative
[/list]
The winners will be announced later this month. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/b3c31ce92f60c60bfb0b18bb63d4cefd848a5fb0.png[/img]

[b]The Future and The Road to 1.7[/b]

We are currently preparing to roll out the 1.7 patch of Blue Prince which marks the completion of a large rollout of accessibility features including Color Assist, Remapping, Cursor Settings, Auto Strolling, and Motion Comfort. While we expect this patch to go live in April, if you would like to test out these features early, feel free to join the patch testing channel in the Laboratory section in our [url=https://discord.gg/BluePrince]discord[/url]! (Obligatory spoiler warning.)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/1f471f2a44b81de0f8e7b01e63b57132d294298b.png[/img]

We have been humbled by the support for Blue Prince over the last year, thank you so much for all the support and enthusiasm,
-Dogubomb and Raw Fury

announcement_body.headline: The Steam Award Nominations are Open Now
announcement_body.body:
The nominations for the Steam Awards 2025 are open now. 

[b]About the Steam Awards[/b]

The Steam Awards are an annual event and a chance for the gaming community to vote for their favourite games in a variety of categories. 

This year’s categories are: 
[list]
[*]Game of the Year
[*]Best Game on Steam Deck
[*]Better with Friends
[*]Outstanding Visual Style
[*]Most Innovative Gameplay
[*]Best Game You Suck At
[*]Best Soundtrack
[*]Outstanding Story-Rich Game
[*]Sit Back & Relax
[/list]
Nominations close on 1 December at 10am PT/6pm GMT.

[b]About Blue Prince[/b]

Blue Prince is a genre-defying atmospheric architectural adventure unlike anything you may have played before. You navigate the shifting corridors and build the manor as you explore room by room, step by step and day by day creating a truly unique gaming experience. Pairing this with the many mysteries and puzzles that Mount Holly holds, finding Room 46 is only the beginning. 

Blue Prince is an IGF, Tribeca, Game Awards, and Golden Joystick nominated game, that launched in April 2025 to near-unanimous critical praise. Gamespot called it "one of the most memorable video game experiences I have ever had”, and The Gamer said “I’ve never played anything like this.” Blue Prince is one of the best reviewed games of 2025 according to Metacritic, with a Metascore of 92.

After eight years of development, the reception of the game has been unreal and humbling.

announcement_body.body:
We are delighted to introduce the Red and Blue Steam Bundle.

The bundle comprises two top-top rated puzzle-adventure titles. Myst (2021), a starkly beautiful island eerily tinged with mystery and shrouded in intrigue and Blue Prince (2025), an atmospheric architectural adventure set within the mysterious Mount Holly estate. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/d2a825ef42c6082c6206dde859939608b531613a.png[/img]

[b][h3]About Myst[/h3][/b]
To learn what happened on the eerie island of Myst you must unravel the mystery you have been thrust into. As you explore and learn you will discover that you are playing a key role in an epic story of ruthless family betrayal where the ending is not yet written…

Myst is a surrealistic adventure game where players must solve puzzles on a journey through an interactive environment, travelling between Ages and learning the story of what happened here and why.

[b][h3]About Red & Blue[/h3][/b]
Whether you are playing Myst or Blue Prince, you will find papers of red and blue scattered throughout the rooms and areas as you explore. But which color should you trust?

[i]Few collaborations feel as full-circle as this one. It was within the ages of Myst that the pages of my imagination were first written. Without Myst, there would be no Blue Prince. And I hope that anyone that hasn’t yet experienced this wonderful world will take a chance and place their hand upon the first page of their next grand adventure. 

-Tonda[/i]

announcement_body.headline: Patch 1.6
announcement_body.body:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/c6fb288ca301a0fdd1868d97da9431c7cf61bc46.png"][/img][/p][p]Hello everyone,

We have released patch [b]1.6[/b] this afternoon for Steam players. This patch addresses a number of issues reported by the community. This update should be available on consoles within a week or two.[/p][p]
The changelog below may include spoilers for some rarer rooms and mechanics.[/p][h3]
[b]Patch 1.6 changelog[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Added ability to manually “restore from backup” to the save menu. This is the same redundant safety system that was implemented in patch [b]1.5 [/b]to automatically restore a backup save in case of file corruption. Manual restoration may be useful for edge cases in which the main file is overwritten but not corrupted (one example may be a platform based cloud save conflict that was resolved incorrectly.) This feature can be found in the Save Menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a softlock that would occur when attempting to use a certain special key in the [spoiler] Vestibule [/spoiler].[/p][/*][*][p]In the [spoiler] Conservatory [/spoiler], controller support now works as intended while [spoiler] resetting rarity using the Room Directory [/spoiler].[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug that has eluded us for a long time that was unintentionally preventing something rare being dug up from dig spots. [i](A scrap of paper containing a hint for contraption components.) [/i]This scrap can only be dug up in a save file where the contraption has not been built and it will only have a chance of appearing later in the game. [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/d09c183989ec231d85856d97d2d5fa3031f8e113.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Hello drafters,
[/p][p]We have released patch 1.5 this afternoon for Steam players. This patch addresses a number of issues reported by the community.   [b]Save Corruption & Loading Freeze Fixes[/b]
[/p][p]We've identified and addressed several edge cases that were causing save file corruption, resulting in a loading freeze when accessing the main menu. Unfortunately, if your save file was affected by these issues, we are sorry to say that means it is corrupted and irretrievable despite our best efforts to find a way to restore it.
[/p][p]This update also includes multiple fixes aimed at preventing these corruption cases from occurring in the future. Several code checks have been added to reduce the chance of corruption including redundant checking of the validity of the save before writing it. Additionally, we’ve implemented an automatic backup system: if the primary save becomes corrupted or lost, a backup save will now load instead.  If you are PS Plus user whose save file has been affected by this, we have had a few encouraging reports from users who were able to restore a backup of their save file via Playstation Plus cloud storage. To restore from cloud on PS5 follow these steps: [/p][p]1.	Go to Settings > Saved Data and Game/App Settings.[/p][p]2.	Select Saved Data (PS5).[/p][p]3.	Choose Download or Delete from Cloud Storage.[/p][p]4.	Select the game and then the specific save file you want to restore.[/p][p]5.	Choose Download. 

We are also currently implementing an “IMPORT TROPHY DATA” feature to work with platform achievements that had been previously earned in previous save files (even if they don’t exist in any of your current save files.) This feature will be included in an upcoming patch.

FURTHER CHANGES IN THIS PATCH LISTED BELOW:[/p][list][*][p]Fixed a bug occurring when consecutive Parlor boxes were opened too quickly.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an input recognition issue on keyboard where \[Right Arrow] and \[A] were incorrectly interpreted as CONFIRM in certain cases.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]Corrected some minor magnification issues and inconsistencies in font usage in the following locations - Library, \[spoiler]Master Bedroom\[/spoiler], \[spoiler]Vault. \[/spoiler]

The method is explained in the Conservatory menu as floorplan rarity can only be reset in the Conservatory).\[/spoiler][/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]\[spoiler]The doors powered by remote power boxes are now opened by button press instead of unlocking automatically. These doors will remain permanently unlocked after being opened.\[/spoiler][/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]\[spoiler]A trunk in the Treasure Trove incorrectly displaying the moon symbol has been changed to the sun symbol. (A blue memo was incorrectly being labeled as false.\[/spoiler][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]We also have corrected a few oversights and bugs in the room drafting logic. Below are listed a few of the resulting technical corrections that may be of interest.
[/p][list][*][p]\[spoiler]Master Bedroom will no longer erroneously appear in places other than the East Wing (Rank 9 related bug)\[/spoiler]
[/p][/*][*][p]\[spoiler]Fixed a narrow bug permitting Foundation to be added to the draft pool after repellent use before 7 days had transpired.\[/spoiler][/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]\[spoiler]Foundation will no longer be drawn with as much frequency on Ranks 2 and 3\[/spoiler]

The patch is live now on Steam. We expect the patch to be available to Xbox and PlayStation players before the weekend. [/p][p][/p][p]Blue Prince is Out Now[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1569580/Blue_Prince/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p][/p][p]

Hello drafters, 

We have released a patch this afternoon to resolve some issues that the community have been experiencing. The patch is now live on Steam and we expect Xbox and PlayStation players to see this before the weekend. As always, the changelog below includes some spoilers. 

[/p][h1]PlayStation 5 Save Rollback Issue[/h1][p]This patch also includes a fix for the PS5 Save Rollback Issue that was preventing players from progressing their explorations of Mount Holly.

This issue was caused by a duplication of save data causing new save information to time out and not be saved. This problem has now been addressed and players should have no issues progressing and saving the game past the point where the bug was initially encountered.

We have worked tirelessly with Sony to avoid any save files being lost once the game patches.However, content that was not saved during the Rollback Issue has unfortunately been lost. Players should be able to return to Mount Holly at the point where they encountered the bug.

[/p][h1]Patch 1.4.5 Changelog:[/h1][list][*][p]Fixed the rollback bug that was interfering with saving the game on PlayStation for some users
[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug occasionally preventing players from entering the highest rank due to a rogue collider.

[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a potential collider softlock that could occur after [spoiler]digging up treasure in the Cloister.[/spoiler][/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a potential collider softlock that could occur after [spoiler]digging up treasure in the Closet.[/spoiler][/p][/*][*][p]The experiment [spoiler]“Gain 1 Key, 1 Gem or 1 Gold (selected at random)” has been changed to “Gain 1 Key, 1 Gem, or 1 Die (selected at random)”[/spoiler][/p][/*][*][p]Unified all instances of "Christoph" to a consistent spelling.

[/p][h1]EVEN DEEPER SPOILER CHANGELOG BELOW[/h1][list][*][p][spoiler]Edited the wording of “Question 33” to provide more clarity. The solution remains unchanged.[/spoiler][/p][/*][*][p][spoiler]Cleaned up the mathematical symbols of “Question 46” to provide more clarity. The solution remains unchanged.[/spoiler][/p][/*][*][p][spoiler]Unified Date formatting in terminal logs for consistency.[/spoiler][/p][/*][*][p][spoiler]Repositioned a (Blue Tents) memo in a ‘found floorplan’ to fix a bug causing it to occasionally not appear. (no content change)[/spoiler][/p][/*][*][p][spoiler]The experiment that “lowers water” will now be replaced with an experiment variation that “raises water” if there is not currently any water to lower.[/spoiler][/p][/*][*][p][spoiler]The experiment “Each time you view your map, lose 10 steps and then” has been changed to “The next 10 times you view your map, lose 10 steps and then”[/spoiler][/p][/*][*][p][spoiler]The experiment “Gain 1 Key for every 40 steps you have” has been changed to “Gain 1 Key for every 30 steps you have”[/spoiler][/p][/*][*][p][spoiler]The experiment “Gain 1 Key, 1 Gem or 1 Gold (selected at random)” has been changed to “Gain 1 Key, 1 Gem, or 1 Die (selected at random)”[/spoiler][/p][/*][*][p][spoiler]On Day One, the trunk in the bedroom will no longer only appear after the first draft.[/spoiler][/p][/*][/list][p]
[spoiler]We would also like to add that we are currently working on a feature to use the Blackbridge Terminal’s “IMPORT TROPHY DATA” feature to work with platform achievements that have been previously earned (even if they don’t exist in any of your current save files.) We expect this feature to be completed soon and will be included in an upcoming patch, thank you for your patience.[/spoiler]

[/p][h1]The Path to 1.10[/h1][p]
It had always been my dream to release a definitive version of the game at launch. I’m a big fan of complete standalone experiences and it was never my plan to continually tinker with the game with regular content updates, room rebalancing, or DLC and the like. Considering this is my first game, I’m extremely proud of everything I managed to include for launch, but there are a few minor things that were not quite completed before our release date that I feel must be added to fulfill that original vision

Those inclusions will be added in [b]1.10[/b], which will be the final major update to the game. It will be the definitive version of the game. 

Among the planned inclusions in this final update: an overhyped arcade game, a curious house cat, accessibility features like color assist mode, controls remapping, cursor size/opacity settings, and widescreen support. Some UI/UX improvements, more variations for end-of-day manor descriptions and accompanying house illustrations, HUD display customization, final room/item balancing, and the addition of a handful of extra cinematics that I am still working on (the unlockable challenge modes actually have their own unique openings and endings!)


NOTE: We will continue to release bug-fixing patches intermittently in the months leading up to 1.10 and some of these updates may preemptively roll out some of the above-mentioned features (we wouldn’t want to sit on accessibility features for months on end while we wait on cinematics!) And while 1.10 will be the last planned content update, we will, of course, continually be committed to fixing bugs for far, far into the future.

[i] - Tonda Ros, Director of Blue Prince[/i]

announcement_body.headline: Dev Blog #3 - Watch Your Steps
announcement_body.body:
In the last [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1569580/view/4196868529807943357]dev blog[/url] we explored the estate of Mount Holly, the mysterious manor where you will spend your time in Blue Prince, examining every room and rumor, day by day…

…and [b]step[/b] by [b]step[/b].

You see, there’s only so much one can do in a single day. Scouring a gigantic estate for clues, after all, can be a very exhausting task.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/e6895df565ad0e3dbdbbc02679f724136808c98f.png[/img]

In Blue Prince, [b]STEPS[/b] represent how much energy you have. You will start every morning with 50 steps, and you will find that number in the top left corner of the screen. But there’s no need to rush! Steps are only lost when moving between rooms. So, you can take your time and spend as much time as you like in each room to explore (and we encourage that!).

And hey, 50 steps to find the 46th room of the house seems perfectly reasonable, right?

[i]Right…?[/i]

Well, let’s just say that you can’t always line up rooms in a straight path to where you are aiming to go. Drafting your house will involve a lot of strategic architectural weaving, unexpected turns, and nasty dead-ends that always seem to pop up at the most inopportune times! If you’re not careful, those steps are going to quickly be depleted as you trek around looking for doors that you passed up earlier in the day. Once you run out of steps, you will have to [i][b]Call it a Day[/b][/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/f7caf54e075945b39eced8b9be0e6fbe452aa4c9.png[/img]

But all hope is not lost! There are several ways to increase your steps whilst inside the manor. Fruit found around the house will give you a quick boost of energy, replenishing a handful of steps, and there are even rooms that you can rest up in to gain even more! One such example is [b]BEDROOM[/b], which will give you [b]+2 STEPS[/b] each time that you enter the room. Quite useful if you draft it in a spot in your house that you plan on traveling through again later.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/b5bbe95e167d5b4fed9fe103b340397f5f3ce72b.png[/img]

If you’re the type of player who loves to explore and wander off the path to investigate and look for secrets, then you may be in need of even more steps than the occasional fruit or bedroom can provide. A room like [b]NURSERY[/b] has the potential to provide a massive amount of steps. That is, if you draft more bedrooms. It is also worth noting that [b]NURSERY[/b] is a dead-end. So if you draft this room in your house you may not have as many options for expansion.

Tough choices lie ahead. You are the architect of your journey to Room 46, choose wisely!

Blue Prince is coming to Steam soon, wishlist now! https://store.steampowered.com/app/1569580/Blue_Prince/

Join us on [url=https://discord.com/invite/BluePrince]Discord[/url]
Follow us on [url=https://x.com/dogubomb]Twitter[/url]

announcement_body.headline: Dev Blog #2 - Mount Holly Estate
announcement_body.body:
[h2][b]Living Wills and Dead Ends[/b][/h2]

Mount Holly, ‘the House of Shifting Rooms’ (as the locals call it), is a sprawling estate resting in the saddle of the Reddington Mountains directly south of the tree line. Once the esteemed domain of your great uncle, Mount Holly now falls under your ownership. Yet an intriguing condition accompanies the inheritance: you must locate the hidden 46th Room of this mysterious 45-room estate.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/1a555432b307102697ead91ffe285e05ff192cec.png[/img]

One of the most interesting features of this unique house is the way the rooms work. In Mount Holly, opening a door does not always lead to the same room. Floorplans shift, things move around and each day the entire blueprint of the house changes. One day you may find a kitchen leading off from the Entrance Hall, the next, a gymnasium. You really can’t take anything for granted.

The central mechanic of Blue Prince is a process that will at once be familiar to both architects and card players called [b]DRAFTING[/b]. When you open a door on the estate, you will be given three potential room options to choose between. As the architect, [i]you[/i] decide from those selections which floorplan you want to build. Each door in Mount Holly is a choice, and the choices you make will shape your adventure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/1b3c25d87dfc4099e2e70faf45cdf2b69536089c.jpg[/img]

Mount Holly provides a wide variety of rooms for you to choose from that range from commonplace to rare. From this pool of rooms, you will progress each day, drafting one room at a time, expanding and exploring the house and its many mysteries as you progress. When you can no longer make progress, for example, if you can’t find any new doors to open, you may [b]‘Call it a Day’[/b] to reset your house and start fresh the next morning with a brand new blueprint.

Mount Holly is an architectural conundrum and there’s so much more about the house we could expand on but I think it’s best if we leave the majority of its many mysterious doors closed… for now.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/f4fbf6485edf89e5fbc09cf0e1c55dba4b3b2f98.png[/img]

We’re really excited for people to soon be able to get hands on with the game, if you’re as hyped as we are we have a [url=https://www.discord.gg/blueprince]Discord[/url] server for all things Blue Prince, join us.

announcement_body.headline: Dev Blog #1 - The Drafting of Blue Prince
announcement_body.body:
[b][h2]Welcome to Mount Holly[/h2][/b]

Are your bags packed yet? Are you ready to begin your search for Room 46? You play as Simon, who has inherited the title and deed to Mount Holly, a puzzling mansion on a sprawling estate. But the inheritance you have received comes with a catch…

[previewyoutube=2cEKyYhC-Eg;full][/previewyoutube]

The debut game of Tonda Ros, a visual artist and independent game developer based out of Hollywood. After a decade of working in the film industry and making stuff for other people, Tonda finally decided in 2016 to make something for himself. The following eight years can only be described as a labour of love.

[i]“This was a project that I initially had expected to be finished in six months. But what’s a year or eight more among friends? I stopped keeping track a while ago.” [/i]- Tonda

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/f21fd7726bdff65239a5208333295cfcd140baea.png[/img]

We sat down with Tonda from Dogubomb to talk about how Blue Prince came to be.

[h3][b]The Idea of Blue Prince[/b][/h3]

[b]Q: When did you come up with the initial idea for Blue Prince?[/b]

A: I had been tinkering for years with a few board game ideas and different design elements that eventually wound up together in the game, but the spring of 2016 was when all these disparate ideas came together under the umbrella of a video game concept.

[b]Q: How did this concept come about?[/b]

A: When I first started learning Unity, my only intention was to casually explore the technology and gauge how difficult it would be to make a game. On my second day in the program, I started working on a first-person test scene because without a character I didn’t need to figure out character animation to get my feet wet. I love first-person games and exploration so I started copy-pasting rooms and made a really big house with a lot of doors. Nothing is more fun to me than being in a room with multiple doors and having to pick one to investigate. That fundamental idea was the core concept I wanted to explore. Choosing between doors and choosing between rooms. I named that first test scene “House of One Hundred Doors”. That was Day Two. It would be another two years before that project was renamed to “Blue Prince”.

[b]Q: Was it always the plan to make the game a mystery strategy game?[/b]

A: I feel like if you let ten people play Blue Prince and then asked them what genre they’d classify the game, you’d get ten different answers. I didn’t try to fit this thing into a box and I’ve noticed players tend to focus on different aspects of the game that appeal to them, which in turn changes their perspective on the game's categorization.

[b]Q: Was this game based on a love of other games like this?[/b]

A: Actually, the game’s inspirational sources are mainly books and board games, but there’s no one wellspring that I heavily drew from. “Blue Prince” is more of a blended combination of a lot of things I love from a lot of different mediums. Speaking as a player, I’m not a big fan of derivative work in games. To me, there’s an extremely fine line between inspiration and imitation. I try my best to stay pretty far away from that line. But over eight years of development, I’m sure I skirted it a few times.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/a43c8638e5e5bcd3ade50403e6f7812f1db0b37b.png[/img]

[h3][b]Making Blue Prince[/b][/h3]

[b]Q: When did development of the game officially start?[/b]

A: At some point during the first three months that original test scene stopped being a test. It evolved and I didn’t have the heart to press B to stop it. Perhaps it was the day I created the first design document and laid out the drafting mechanic. Perhaps it was the day I first let a friend play a build and saw the look of disbelief on their face. Or maybe it was the day I quit “my job” to focus on the game full time. It was sometime in 2016.

[b]Q: Was this with the same team as Dogubomb has now?[/b]

A: I was working completely solo for the first two years. So no, the Blue Prince team was formed very slowly, piece by piece over the course of the project and the roster has changed many times over.

[b]Q: What were the main challenges in making the game?[/b]

A: By far, the biggest hurdle was maintaining mental stamina throughout such a long, long project. I worked about 80 hours a week on average, which I think is only sustainable if you really love what you are doing and don’t really know how much longer it’s going to take! Throughout development, I always believed the game was one year away from being complete. It’s easy to run in the desert when you see water. It doesn’t matter how dehydrated or tired you are. If you see water, you’re up and running. That’s what it was like. The game’s finish line was an ever-motivating, ever-moving goalpost that was always just out of reach, like a mirage on the desert horizon.

[b]Q: What were some of your favourite parts of the development process?[/b]

A: This one’s really easy to answer. Without a doubt my favorite thing in the process has been watching playtesters play the game. It's hard to imagine a game developer answering anything else honestly. The amount of joy I get from watching people play is ridiculous. I felt the same way at GDC watching people finally getting to experience the game.I think it helps that everyone’s playthrough is so unique. I’m constantly being surprised by things players are coming up with and the individual way they each approach the challenges of the game. It really never gets old.

[b]Q: How are you feeling about the fact the game will launch soon?[/b]

A: Thirsty!

announcement_body.headline: Welcome to Mt. Holly
announcement_body.body:
Welcome Drafters,  

We were delighted to see the trailer for Blue Prince shown at the Future Game Show this evening. If you missed it, you can check it out here:  

[previewyoutube=2cEKyYhC-Eg;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]What is Blue Prince? [/h1]
Blue Prince is a genre-defying mystery strategy puzzle adventure unlike anything you’ve ever played before.  

You play as Simon, the sole beneficiary of the Sinclair Estate at Mount Holly, a sprawling 45-room Manor set in beautiful and expansive grounds. Your grand-uncle: Herbert S Sinclair, recently passed away and you travel to Mount Holly to claim your inheritance. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/b90b333febe8b0a863833a87d95b7668ec2dd35e.jpg[/img]

But it’s not going to be that simple… 

Herbert was a mysterious and enigmatic man when he was alive, and he has left his biggest challenge yet for you to solve: Find the hidden Room 46 in the 45-room Estate.  

Mount Holly’s shifting nature means that traversing through its halls is an unpredictable journey where no two days play out the same. You also cannot take for granted what room awaits behind any door, floorplans change daily, and every day you start completely from scratch. 

Can you solve the mystery of Mount Holly and find what awaits within Room 46? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40356052/1b3c25d87dfc4099e2e70faf45cdf2b69536089c.jpg[/img]

[h2]A note from the developer [/h2]
[i]“We’re thrilled to finally have Blue Prince formally introduced to the world. This has been a journey (and house) 8 years in the making, and we can’t wait to unlock the doors of Mount Holly soon and welcome you into our world.”  - [b]Tonda, Director of Blue Prince[/b] [/i]
